case_title.quote: BADAL MURMU AND ORS. V. STATE OF WEST BENGAL
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

accused_gender.quote: The women who had assembled there also assaulted the wives, mother and sister
accused_gender.reason: Accused are implicitly male, distinguished from the women who assaulted; no explicit statement, but supported.

accused_age.reason: No age of any accused is stated.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not stated.

accused_caste.reason: Judgment states Santhal community and tribal status of appellants.

accused_occupation.reason: No occupation of accused is stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: They come from a very poor strata of the society
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment describes accused as very poor and economically weak.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: stealing of the hen by her husband
victim_gender.reason: Victim is the husband of the first wife, so male.

victim_caste.correct_value: Not explicitly stated; implied Santhal community (wives are Santhal material witnesses)
victim_caste.quote: The appellants as well as the material witnesses belong to Santhal community.
victim_caste.reason: Caste of victim is not stated directly, though the material witnesses (victim's wives) are Santhal.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The appellants and the prosecution witnesses belong to Santhal Community of village Mobarakpur.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Supported: fellow villagers of same community with prior inimical dealings.

offence_category.quote: convicted for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
offence_category.reason: Final conviction is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

statutory_provisions.quote: conviction of the appellants for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC is quashed
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 148, 302/149 and 304 Part II are all supported.

weapon.quote: some of the appellants had tangies in their hand. PW-1 Nilmoni stated that some of them had tangies but they did not use them.
weapon.reason: Lathis used; tangies carried but not used, as stated.

evidence_type.quote: The doctor ... stated that the death was caused due to the injuries
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness testimony and post-mortem evidence are the evidence relied on.

confession.quote: The accused denied the prosecution case.
confession.reason: No confession; accused denied the prosecution case.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: It is true that there were also two rib fractures and haemotoma under the scalp.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Death, fourteen injuries, rib fractures and haematoma are stated; court did not weigh them as aggravating.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: It is an unusual case where a trivial incident led to a murder.
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Trivial trigger, unused tangies, poverty and long custody are all stated.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under s.148 and s.302/149 and imposed life imprisonment.

high_court_outcome.quote: The appellants' appeal was dismissed by the High Court.
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeal, confirming conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.quote: the impugned order is modified to the above extent
final_outcome.reason: Conviction was modified by the Supreme Court.

offence_finally_established.quote: convicted for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
offence_finally_established.reason: Finally established offence is culpable homicide under s.304 Part II.

imprisonment_type.quote: the sentence already undergone by them is directed to be treated as sentence imposed on them
imprisonment_type.reason: No fresh imprisonment; time already undergone treated as sentence.

imprisonment_years.reason: No specific term of years is stated.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Earlier assault on the second man is described without naming the weapon; the judgment does not say sticks were used then.
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but the claim that the second man was assaulted with sticks is not supported; weapon is unspecified.

offence_severity.reason: No offence severity classification is stated.

attempt_completion.reason: Offence completed with death of the victim.

physical_harm.quote: the doctor noticed fourteen injuries on the deceased. Most of them were bruises and abrasions.
physical_harm.reason: Death, fourteen injuries, fractures and haematoma are all stated.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Two offences charged (s.148; s.302 r/w s.149). s.302/149 conviction set aside and replaced by s.304 Part II; s.148 not expressly addressed.
number_of_offences.quote: the conviction of the appellants for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC is quashed and set aside. Instead, they are convicted for culpable homicide
number_of_offences.reason: Charge count is right, but s.304 Part II was a substitution, not an upheld conviction.

financial_property_loss.quote: he was ordered to give a hen to appellant-B and, in addition, he had to give two handies of liquor.
financial_property_loss.reason: Theft of hen and penalty of hen and liquor are supported.

premeditation_planning.quote: the attendant circumstances do not indicate that the appellants shared any common object to kill
premeditation_planning.reason: Court found no shared intent to kill; blows in a frenzy, consistent with the value.

motive.quote: It appears that they were no( happy with the penalty imposed by the Salishman.
motive.reason: Motive is anger at the community penalty over the hen theft.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The evidence of PW-1 Nilmoni, PW-3 Rabi Soren, PW-6 Sumi Soren and PW-7 Kanka is truthful
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Ocular testimony and PW-9's blunt-object opinion are accepted as stated.

witness_credibility.quote: PW-7 Kanka did not hesitate to name his brother as one of the assailants.
witness_credibility.reason: Witnesses found truthful, rustic, related but not falsely implicating.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No accused post-offence conduct is stated; the flight concerns the witness PW-7.

custody_duration.quote: we are informed that the appellants are in jail for almost 14 years
custody_duration.reason: Matches the judgment's statement of nearly 14 years.

trial_duration.quote: On the next day, in the morning, deceased-Jhore Soren and PW-7 Kanka were called
trial_duration.reason: Incident date and High Court and Supreme Court dates match the judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Vibha Datta Makhija, Ruchi Agnihotri for the Appellants. Anip Sachthey, Kabir S. Bose, Shagun Matta, Saakaar Sardana for the Respondents.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names and roles match the judgment.

investigation_status.quote: PW-1 Nilmoni ... rushed to Memari Police Station and gave her statement.
investigation_status.reason: Complaint, investigation, charges and 10 witnesses are stated.

appeal_history.quote: The appellants' appeal was dismissed by the High Court. Hence, the present appeal.
appeal_history.reason: Appeal history across trial, High Court and Supreme Court is accurate.

prosecution_argument.quote: the appellants who were members of the unlawful assembly knew that the murder was likely to be committed
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution's common-object and intent arguments are accurately stated.

defence_argument.quote: the appellants are poor tribals; they are in jail for a considerably long time
defence_argument.reason: Defence arguments on acquittal and s.304 Part II are accurately stated.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Common object under s.149 must be established on the facts; individual roles and the fatal injury must be considered; absent intention to kill, s.304 Part II applies.
legal_principle_applied.quote: It is not, therefore, known as to which is the fatal injury.
legal_principle_applied.reason: The court did not treat the injuries as non-fatal; the doctor said all injuries led to death.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sukhdev Singh v. State of Punjab (AIR 1992 SC 755); Sarman & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1993 Supp. (2) SCC 356)
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All listed precedents and citations appear in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.quote: justice must be tempered with mercy
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale matches the court's reasoning on poverty, trivial cause, and time served.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: their anger and reaction to the theft of hen must be viewed against the background of their economic and social status
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Mitigating factors match the court's stated reasoning.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: there can be no justification for the appellants' actions
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court noted no justification but weighed no aggravating factor.

other_sentence_order.quote: They are directed to be released forthwith unless they are otherwise required in any other case.
